steps: This video shows how checkpointing lets a long agent task survive a crash. Worker A takes ticket T one thousand and one, a twenty step job: classify, research the knowledge base, fix, and verify.
Workers can crash mid-task. Right now the task state lives only in memory, so a crash at step fifteen throws away fourteen finished steps and starts again at step one.
So after every step, Worker A now saves a checkpoint to shared storage: the current step, the message history, and metadata.
Steps two to fourteen repeat the same beat: ask Claude, read the result, save the checkpoint. After step fourteen, the store holds the full state.
Then Worker A dies at step fifteen. This time the loss is only the one step in progress, not fourteen.
A fresh, stateless Worker B starts up and asks shared storage for the checkpoint. It gets the state after step fourteen, so it resumes at step fifteen.

Worker B re-runs step fifteen, which is safe because each step is idempotent. The takeaway: save state outside the worker, and make steps safe to repeat. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
